key_insight: Detonation-sprayed AlCuFe quasicrystalline coatings form a thermally hardening, oxidation-resistant barrier whose phase evolution under 450°C helps sustain protection over 250 h.
engineering_relevance: This coating approach could extend the high-temperature oxidation life of TC4 titanium alloys by maintaining mechanical stability while limiting scale growth.
method: Fabricated AlCuFe quasicrystalline coatings by detonation spraying (DS).
Aged/oxidized coatings in air at 450°C for up to 250 h.
Tracked oxidation kinetics, phase evolution, and microhardness changes over time.
evidence_signal: The coating followed parabolic oxidation kinetics with kp = 1.83 × 10^-2 mg²·cm^-4·h^-1, while microhardness increased from 491 HV0.2 to 665.2 HV0.2 after 250 h.
watch_item: Long-term performance depends on phase stability during Al depletion, so processing control is important to avoid excessive decomposition of the quasicrystalline phase.
paper_title: High-temperature oxidation kinetics and microstructural evolution of detonation-sprayed AlCuFe quasicrystalline coatings
